No generator produces this file or reads it; see docs/RUNTIME_DATA_MODELS.md section '## 17. Stash Special Tabs & the Crafting Route' for the full write-up and ForgePact issue #14 (ForgePact/docs/crafting-materials-research.md) for the research.

materials.cell_path_note: the array being two-level is measured; the [x][y] axis order is from the static reading, not itself probed live

save.second_argument_note: as the close supplied it; its meaning is not measured

crafting_cube.note: whether the game's own count walks this grid is not observed; the grid's persistence across a save does not gate the build, per the owner's design (2026-09-24): only the craft's own items are placed here, at the press, and consumed at once

bag_to_stash_move.note: The routines the game's own Ctrl + left click runs to move one item from the bag into the stash tab on show, in that order, and the shapes that reproduced the move by name (ForgePact #68). Self and other are the two UI_Inventory_Grid_obj nodes told apart by uiNodeCallstack: InventoryGrid (the bag's, rebinding to the bag view on show) and StashGrid (the stash's, rebinding to the tab on show). The Socketable tab merges by name (socket_merge, Live 1f and 1g); placing a kind it does not hold yet was moved by hand only and has no by-name shape.

validate.arguments: the item struct; called again after the placement with self the StashGrid node
validate.answer: empty text, a refusal included (the Socketable tab's refusal of jewels shows nothing in it)

stack.arguments: the shown tab's cell array; 0 and 13 into the personal page, 9 and 2 into a shared page, the Materials tab and the Socketable tab; the item struct; the count to merge (1 on every hand move; the whole count merged by name); a small number (0 on a page and the Materials tab, 8 on the Socketable tab)
stack.answer: true after merging into a stack of the item's identity on that array with room for the count (stack_cap); false when there is none, and then the grid placement follows

stack_cap.rule: StashAddToStack takes its cap from its sixth argument: 999 when it lacks flag 8 (0 on the pages and the Materials tab), 999999 when it carries it (8 on the Socketable tab). It walks the array in order and merges into the first stack of the item's identity whose count plus the moved count stays at or below the cap, answering true; a stack that would pass the cap is passed over, and with none left it answers false. The whole count or none: a stack is never topped up with part of an item. The Materials tab holds several stacks of one kind, the Socketable tab one per kind (the owner, 2026-09-30). Not read: whether the count added is the fifth argument or the item's own o, and the walk order beyond array order. Measured (Live 3, 2026-09-30) for the 999 cap on the Materials tab through ForgePact's Move all: beside a kind's one stack of 875, a unit of 125 was placed as a new stack in a free cell and the 875 left unchanged, and a unit of 129 then passed over the 875 and merged into the stack of 125 (254); no stack read above 999. The 999999 cap with flag 8 remains a static reading
stack_cap.source: ForgePact #131; ForgePact/docs/stash-move-research.md, Static reading 4 (2026-09-30) and Live 3 results (material-overflow, material-partial)

grid.arguments: the shown tab's cell array (the StashGrid node's nodeGrid on a page, Controller_obj.stashMaterialTab on the Materials tab), the item struct, 0, undefined
grid.answer: a struct of tabNumber, x, y, tabType, success; success=false when that array has no room, and no other tab is tried; tabNumber read 0 on shared page 1 too

source_clear.arguments: the item's anchor cell node in the bag grid's nodeGrid, read [y][x], then undefined; after a by-name placement (which leaves the item in its bag cells) or a merge, while the item is still on map 0 and before the owner step

socket_merge.container: the Socketable tab has no one array: one UI_Inventory_Grid_obj per item on the tab, its uiNodeCallstack StashSocketGrid, its nodeGrid one cell holding that item, whose key answers on map 9 (Controller_obj.stashSocketItemSlot is not the container); saved in stash.hss under socket_tab
socket_merge.arguments: the nodeGrid of the StashSocketGrid node holding the item's identity; 9; 2; the item struct; its count (1 measured); 8. Self and other the bag's grid node with its Socket view on show; no ValidateItem before it. Then source_clear on the bag cell, only after that node's item's o rose by exactly the count
socket_merge.answer: true, the node's o rising by the count (an orb, base id 118: 81 to 82, twice); a gem (base id 38) merged the same way and gained o=2, so no non-stackable answer was met on this tab. A whole stack merges too: a unit of 3 of the orb, merged through ForgePact's Move all, raised the node's o by exactly 3, 92 to 95 (Live 3, 2026-09-30, ForgePact #131)

owner_step.arguments: 0, 9, the item's key as text; only after a placement the re-read confirmed (alone, on an item still in the bag, it leaves the key on no map)

shared.map: not established: after the owner step the key answers on neither map 0 nor map 9 by GetItemFromFingerprint, as every shared-page key does

materials.owner_step: 0 to 9 for a new identity; none for a merge

socketable.owner_step: none for a merge (by name, Live 1f and 1g); 0 to 9 for a new identity, by hand only (Live 1e)

cases: a class-10 item by hand and by name into the personal page and shared page 1, and against the full shared page 2
a new material identity by hand and by name into the Materials tab, one-unit and whole-stack (15) merges
a rune, a gem and an orb into the Socketable tab by hand; jewels and an Incarnation Gem refused by the game
an orb (base id 118) and a gem (base id 38) merged by name into their StashSocketGrid nodes on the Socketable tab, count 1

ui_node_api.note: The game's own UI node routines, as the in-game Move all button uses them (ForgePact #68). Measured in Live 1f and 1g unless an entry says R, a static reading. A node's click is its user event 15, run from the owning window's Step with self the node, other the window and one argument, the node's activationArgs, handed to its activationFunc; with activationFunc undefined the event does nothing (R; measured in Live 1g only that no armed routine logged a call with such a node as self and no dialog appeared).

sort_node.activation: gml_Script_InventorySortTab, bound with the Sort node itself as self; activationArgs [1]

ui_node_api.node_origin: UiCreateNode's x and y are the new node's origin, not its top-left (M, Live 1f and 1g, the same numbers both times; ForgePact #131): for UI_Button_Small_obj (sprite Menu_Button_Chat_spr) the origin lies at its bbox centre (made at 2113.1, 1198.9, bbox 2016.2, 1176.1, 2211.9, 1221.7), while the Sort node's origin is its bbox top-left (2303.5, 1198.9, bbox 2303.5, 1198.9, 2485.9, 1261.6), at a 2560x1440 GUI. The Sort node is a UI_Button_Small_obj too, drawn with Inventory_Tab_Button_Solid_spr, so the origin follows the sprite, not the object. Live 3 (2026-09-30) read the same relation at another GUI scale: the node made at 2178.0, 1295.0 read the bbox 2076.0, 1271.0, 2282.0, 1319.0, and Sort sat at 2290.0, 1262.0 with the bbox 2290.0, 1262.0, 2482.0, 1328.0. The width, 195.7 in Live 1f and 1g, is not a whole sprite size (a GUI scale is in play), so a node's extents about its origin are read from the node, not its sprite, and on a later frame once it is visible and its box reads the same twice, not in the frame it was made

mercenary_button.name: UI_Button_Open_Mercenary_obj
mercenary_button.listed: Only with the bag open on its own (the C key). With the stash open menulayout lists none, and after the stash's close neither it nor InventorySort is listed (Live 5 alone: Live 6 ran no Mercenary query with the stash open or after a close)
mercenary_button.box_relation: Relative to InventorySort's bbox: its left edge 196/192 of Sort's width left of Sort's left edge, the same top, Sort's width and height, so its right edge is 4 GUI units short of Sort's left. Read 2094,1262,2286,1328 beside Sort's 2290,1262,2482,1328 at a 2560x1440 GUI in Live 5 and again in Live 6; InventorySort's box is the same with the stash open. One GUI scale only

label_members.label_place: Inferred, not measured: the label's left edge sat at the node's x plus drawXOffset (Sort: 2290 + 48 = 2338, its label box's left edge; the node within 2: 2094 + 48 = 2142 against 2140 in Live 6, 2090 + 48 = 2138 against 2136 in Live 5). Vertically the label is centred in the box (top 1286 with the node at y 1262 and drawYOffset 9), and which member places it vertically is not separated; the 13 were written together, so none is shown to place it on either axis. A UiCreateNode button already wearing Sort's sprite and scale differed from InventorySort in exactly these 13 writable members, besides its identity, place, text and activation; with them copied from Sort by name (and Sort's sprite_index and scale) the node's label is drawn centred in its box like Sort's
label_members.kinds: textFont reads as an asset reference (ref font __newfont2 on Sort); dropShadow and the four navi* flags as bools; the rest as numbers
label_members.absolute_members: createX, navBboxX and navBboxY hold an absolute GUI position (on Sort, its box's corner). Written raw as Sort's onto a node 200 units to its left in Live 5 and 196 in Live 6, the label was still drawn inside the node's own box
label_members.persist: Copied onto the node and read back equal at once (Live 5), and again equal to Sort's in a probe diff seconds later and on a node made after a close and reopen (Live 6)
label_members.not_established: which of the 13 places the label on either axis (they were written together); what the navi* flags and navBbox* members do beyond the label, such as gamepad navigation; whether the game rewrites any of them in longer play

create.arguments: x; y; the object index; the activation (undefined leaves activationFunc undefined); the call-stack name, stored as the node's uiNodeCallstack. Self and other the window that will own the node. Answers the node (visible 0 that frame, 1 the next)

remove.arguments: the node; self the window that owns it. The window's own close destroys a node still in its list; a tab switch keeps it

set_activation.arguments: the node; a script, bound as a method whose self is the node when callable, else activationFunc left undefined. A node bound to UiSetFloatingToFalse ended the game when clicked (that script is written for another object)
set_activation.measured: M (the dispatch and the crash); the binding rule R

move.arguments: the node; x; y. Sets both and runs the node's own position update

cases: one Materials-tab entry the bag stacks (Greater Unstable Dust, class 14, b=51)
one Socketable stack of 10 (Pristine Ruby, class 15, b=51)
